text.p: These are the leading stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Sierra Leone military junta attacks Nigerian ECOMOG soldiers in Freetown.
- Rail services between Lagos and northern Nigeria will be paralysed for some time after the stalling of restoration work at southwestern Ibadan due to a derailment.
- Anxiety has gripped Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation over the need to extend imports of fuel after September.
- Petroleum industry analysts have faulted the finance ministry for failing to release $200 million approved for the repair of refineries.
- Manufacturers Association of Nigeria warns that the economy may experience negative growth this year due to a persistent liquidity squeeze.

- World Bank officials say that talks with Nigeria on a medium-term economic programme have not been dropped, only that they have hit an impasse because of Nigeria's delay in privatising utilities and scrapping a dual exchange rate mechanism.
- Canada's Abacan Resources has borrowed $35 million overseas to pay for operations by Nigeria's Amni International, one of several local partners in oil production.
